regions.Bluegrass and Bourbon Country: Horse farms, distilleries and Shakers: Lexington's Keeneland and Horse Park, Frankfort's capitol and Buffalo Trace, Bardstown, Lincoln's birthplace and a night at Shaker Village.
regions.Cave Country: Mammoth Cave deserves a full day of tours (book ahead); add the Corvette Museum and the boat ride at Lost River Cave in Bowling Green.
regions.Eastern Kentucky Mountains: Arches of the Red River Gorge and Natural Bridge, crafts in Berea, Cumberland Falls and the Wilderness Road at Cumberland Gap.
regions.Louisville and the Ohio River: Museum Row on Main Street, the Speed, Churchill Downs and Old Louisville's Victorian streets, with Madison and Clifty Falls upriver on the Indiana side.
regions.Southern Illinois and the Lower Ohio: Sandstone country in the Shawnee National Forest, cypress swamps on the Cache River, then across the Ohio to Paducah's quilt museum and Land Between the Lakes. Best in October.

sites.name: Mammoth Cave National Park
sites.desc: The longest known cave system in the world, more than 400 miles surveyed. A UNESCO World Heritage Site.

sites.name: National Corvette Museum
sites.desc: Next to the Bowling Green Corvette plant, known for the 2014 sinkhole that swallowed eight cars.

sites.name: Lost River Cave
sites.desc: An underground boat tour on a cave river in Bowling Green.

sites.name: Shaker Museum at South Union
sites.desc: The westernmost Shaker community, with an 1824 dwelling house and museum.

sites.name: Abraham Lincoln Birthplace National Historical Park
sites.desc: John Russell Pope's 1911 memorial temple encloses a symbolic cabin near Hodgenville.
sites.wiki: Abraham Lincoln Birthplace National Historical Park

sites.name: My Old Kentucky Home State Park
sites.desc: Federal Hill in Bardstown, associated with Stephen Foster's song.
sites.wiki: My Old Kentucky Home State Park

sites.name: Oscar Getz Museum of Whiskey History
sites.desc: Bardstown museum of American whiskey from the colonial era through Prohibition.
sites.wiki: Oscar Getz Museum of Whiskey History

sites.name: Maker's Mark Distillery
sites.desc: A National Historic Landmark distillery in a Victorian campus at Loretto, with Chihuly glass in its cellars.

sites.name: Abbey of Gethsemani
sites.desc: The Trappist monastery where Thomas Merton lived and wrote.
sites.wiki: Abbey of Our Lady of Gethsemani

sites.name: Buffalo Trace Distillery
sites.desc: A National Historic Landmark distillery on the Kentucky River in Frankfort with free tours.

sites.name: Woodford Reserve Distillery
sites.desc: Limestone distillery buildings of the 1830s among horse farms near Versailles.

sites.name: Kentucky State Capitol
sites.desc: A 1910 Beaux-Arts capitol in Frankfort with a floral clock on its lawn.

sites.name: Thomas D. Clark Center for Kentucky History
sites.desc: The Kentucky Historical Society's museum in Frankfort.

sites.name: Shaker Village of Pleasant Hill
sites.desc: The largest restored Shaker community in the country, with more than 30 original buildings.

sites.name: Old Fort Harrod State Park
sites.desc: A reconstruction of the first permanent settlement in Kentucky (1774) at Harrodsburg.

sites.name: Perryville Battlefield
sites.desc: Site of the largest Civil War battle in Kentucky, fought in 1862.

sites.name: Camp Nelson National Monument
sites.desc: A Union supply depot that became a major recruiting center for Black soldiers and a refuge for their families.

sites.name: Kentucky Horse Park
sites.desc: Working horse farm and park in Lexington with the International Museum of the Horse.

sites.name: Keeneland
sites.desc: Lexington's limestone racecourse; morning workouts are open to watch.

sites.name: Ashland, the Henry Clay Estate
sites.desc: The rebuilt Italianate home of statesman Henry Clay in Lexington.

sites.name: Mary Todd Lincoln House
sites.desc: Mary Todd's girlhood home in Lexington, the first site restored to honor a first lady.

sites.name: Kentucky Derby Museum at Churchill Downs
sites.desc: The museum of the Kentucky Derby, with track tours under the twin spires.

sites.name: Speed Art Museum
sites.desc: Kentucky's oldest and largest art museum, founded in 1927.

sites.name: Muhammad Ali Center
sites.desc: Riverfront museum on Ali's life, boxing career and principles.

sites.name: Frazier History Museum
sites.desc: History museum on Museum Row, and the official starting point of the Kentucky Bourbon Trail.

sites.name: Louisville Slugger Museum and Factory
sites.desc: Factory tour of the famous baseball bats, marked by a giant bat leaning on the building.

sites.name: KMAC Contemporary Art Museum
sites.desc: Contemporary art and craft museum on Main Street.

sites.name: 21c Museum Hotel Louisville
sites.desc: The original 21c, a hotel that doubles as a free contemporary art museum.

sites.name: Kentucky Science Center
sites.desc: Hands-on science museum in a row of cast-iron facades.

sites.name: Big Four Bridge
sites.desc: A former railroad truss bridge turned walkway between Louisville and Jeffersonville.

sites.name: Belle of Louisville
sites.desc: The oldest operating Mississippi-style steamboat, with cruises on the Ohio.

sites.name: Old Louisville
sites.desc: One of the largest Victorian residential neighborhoods in the country, best seen on foot around St. James Court.

sites.name: Conrad-Caldwell House
sites.desc: A Richardsonian Romanesque mansion on St. James Court, open as a museum.

sites.name: Thomas Edison House
sites.desc: The shotgun cottage where young Edison boarded while a telegraph operator.

sites.name: Locust Grove
sites.desc: A Georgian farm house of the 1790s, the last home of George Rogers Clark.

sites.name: Cave Hill Cemetery
sites.desc: A landscaped Victorian cemetery and arboretum, burial place of Colonel Sanders.

sites.name: Bernheim Arboretum and Research Forest
sites.desc: Arboretum and forest south of Louisville, with Thomas Dambo's wooden Forest Giants and a canopy walk.

sites.name: Red River Gorge
sites.desc: Sandstone cliffs and more than a hundred natural arches in the Daniel Boone National Forest.

sites.name: Natural Bridge State Resort Park
sites.desc: A 78 foot sandstone arch with a skylift, next to the Red River Gorge.

sites.name: Kentucky Artisan Center, Berea
sites.desc: Showcase of Kentucky crafts in Berea, the state's folk arts and crafts capital.

sites.name: Cumberland Falls State Resort Park
sites.desc: A wide waterfall known for its moonbow on clear nights near the full moon.

sites.name: Cumberland Gap National Historical Park
sites.desc: The mountain pass of the Wilderness Road, with the Pinnacle Overlook over three states.

sites.name: Kentucky Coal Mining Museum
sites.desc: Museum in a company commissary in Benham, with a walk-in mine nearby.

sites.name: Bluegrass Music Hall of Fame and Museum
sites.region: Southern Illinois and the Lower Ohio
sites.desc: Owensboro museum of bluegrass, the music named for Kentucky.

sites.name: National Quilt Museum
sites.region: Southern Illinois and the Lower Ohio
sites.desc: Contemporary and traditional quilts in Paducah, a UNESCO Creative City of Crafts and Folk Art.

sites.name: Land Between the Lakes
sites.region: Southern Illinois and the Lower Ohio
sites.desc: A long peninsula between Kentucky Lake and Lake Barkley with an elk and bison prairie.
sites.wiki: Land Between the Lakes National Recreation Area

sites.name: Wickliffe Mounds
sites.region: Southern Illinois and the Lower Ohio
sites.desc: A Mississippian village site near the confluence of the Ohio and Mississippi.
